name: Baryon number is not constrained by spatial closure

source.located: No originating paper; the tree cites none (permute.py:132-134, :343-347, :562-564 carry no reference). The claim is the conjunction of two standard results. (i) U(1)_B is a global, ungauged symmetry of the Standard Model, so no Gauss constraint acts on it. Textbook folklore, NAMED-NOT-READ. (ii) B is not even exactly conserved: the 't Hooft anomaly/instanton result (1976, NAMED-NOT-READ as a classic). READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT in Matchev & Verner arXiv:2505.05607v1 p.6 eq.(48), Tye & Wong arXiv:1710.07223v1 p.1 and p.5, and Tye & Wong arXiv:1505.03690v3 p.2. The closed-universe/global-symmetry literature was located by WebSearch only and is NAMED-NOT-READ: Harlow-Usatyuk-Zhao arXiv:2501.02359 and the baby-universe discussion at arXiv:2004.06738. The same goes for the torsion-balance bounds on B- and B-L-coupled long-range forces (arXiv:1207.2442, 2101.02096, 1606.08374).

published_statement: No single published statement is the tree's source (see source.located). READ restatements of the anomaly limb, verbatim. 2505.05607v1 p.6: 'In the Standard Model (or any non-Abelian gauge theory with chiral fermions), the baryon number current J^mu_B is not conserved at the quantum level due to the chiral anomaly [1-3]. Instead, it satisfies an anomaly equation of the form d_mu J^mu_B = N_f g^2/(32 pi^2) Tr(W W~) (48), where N_f = 3 is the number of fermion families' ... 'An instanton with winding number N mediates a tunneling process between states with different baryon numbers: |n> -> |n+N>, where the change in baryon number is Delta B = 3N for the Standard Model with three fermion generations.' 1710.07223v1 p.1: 'It is well known that the baryon number B and the lepton number L are not conserved in the electroweak theory [2, 3]. ... (B + L)-violating processes ... where Delta B = Delta L = 3 Delta n.' 1710.07223v1 p.5: 'Going from n = 0 ... to n = 1 ... implies that the universe goes from a vacuum with baryon number B = 0 to another vacuum with baryon number B = 3.' 1505.03690v3 p.2: 'both the baryon number (B) and the lepton numbers (L) are not conserved in the standard electroweak theory because of the presence of anomalies [1-4] and instantons [5]. The non-Abelian nature of a Yang-Mills theory leads to a topologically non-trivial vacuum structure.' The tree's statement is 'no topological constraint; not forced' (permute.py:346) and 'nor for baryon number, which is not forced at all' (permute.py:134).
published_hypotheses: H1 Standard-Model field content: U(1)_B is a global symmetry with no gauge field. B1 shows it CANNOT be gauged with SM fermions, because A[SU(2)^2 B] = +1/2 and A[Y^2 B] = -1/2 per generation. Adding nu_R does not rescue it.

H2 No additional gauged U(1) under which B (or B-L) is charged with a massless, untwisted gauge boson. With one nu_R per generation U(1)_{B-L} is anomaly-free (B1, all six coefficients 0) and CAN be gauged. If it were, massless and untwisted, the sibling Gauss theorem would force total B-L = 0, and so B = L, on a closed slice. Massive (Higgsed) B-L does not force the total (B5, Proca mechanism).

H3 'Total B' means the net fermion-number integral. In the SM it is not conserved: d(B)/dt = N_f d(N_CS)/dt (+ hypercharge term), so Delta B = Delta L = 3 Delta n (READ 1710.07223 p.1; B2). Only B-L is exactly conserved perturbatively and nonperturbatively in the SM.

H4 Classical or semiclassical QFT on a fixed closed spatial slice. Nonperturbative quantum-gravity statements about closed universes (one-dimensional Hilbert space; no global symmetries) are outside this frame (NAMED-NOT-READ).

H5 (what 'not forced' means) closure imposes no constraint on the VALUE of total B. It does not mean B is topologically trivial. In the Skyrme realisation B is the degree of a map from the closed slice to SU(2) = S^3, an integer quantised by topology (B3). Anomalous changes of B are locked to the Chern-Simons winding (B2).
hypothesis_drift: OVERSTATED 'no topological constraint' at permute.py:346. The core boolean (closure does not force B, CONSTRAINED_BY_CLOSURE[2][1] = False) is re-derived (B3 and B4). The gloss 'no topological constraint' is wider than true on two counts, each computed here. (a) Anomalous changes of B are topologically locked to Chern-Simons winding: Delta B = N_f Delta N_CS = 3 (B2; READ 2505.05607 p.6, 1710.07223 p.1). (b) In the Skyrme realisation B is a topological degree, integer-quantised on a closed slice (B3: the full eps Tr(LLL) density matches the hedgehog reduction to 5e-18; degree n for n = -3..3 on R^3 u {inf} and n = 0..4 on S^3). Topology constrains B's quantisation and its changes, not its value. 'Not forced' stands; 'no topological constraint' does not.

UNNAMED H1/H2 at the owner sites permute.py:132-134, :346 and :562-564. None of them says why B is not forced. The canonical entry's hypothesis 'baryon number has no associated Gauss-law gauge field' comes from the extractor and is not in permute.py. The operative premise is 'no gauged U(1) acting on B (or B-L) with a massless untwisted boson'. It holds in the SM (B1: B is anomalous, so it cannot be gauged). It fails in any extension with a massless gauged B-L (anomaly-free with nu_R, B1). There closure would force B_total = L_total, which is a constraint on B though not B = 0. Observationally the premise is bounded by torsion-balance tests of B and B-L-coupled long-range forces, not established (1207.2442, 2101.02096; NAMED-NOT-READ). That is the same logical shape as the sibling's photon-mass premise.

The tree's own baryon row contradicts the universal reading. Baryon number takes either sign (baryons.py:55-56: '+1 on every particle here and -1 on every antiparticle'), yet it is not constrained by closure (permute.py:346). Sign-indefiniteness is necessary for a zero-total constraint to be non-vacuous, but it is not sufficient: the sufficient mechanism is a Gauss constraint from a massless gauge field (B4: the same integer lattice, total != 0 UNSAT with the Gauss constraint, total = 1 SAT without it). The direction apply.py:252 actually uses, sign-committed => not constrained (energy), is untouched. permute.py:137's modal 'CAN constrain' is consistent. apply.py:91's 'IS CONSTRAINED' is not.

rederivation.outcome: ALL CHECKS PASS (38 checks, ~1.5 s; sympy 1.14.0, z3 5.1.0). B1: exact SM anomaly coefficients per generation, left-handed Weyl basis. Sanity guard: the four hypercharge anomalies cancel. U(1)_B has SU(3)^2 B = 0, SU(2)^2 B = +1/2, Y^2 B = -1/2 and grav B = B^3 = Y B^2 = 0. So B is anomalous and cannot be gauged with SM content, even with nu_R. U(1)_{B-L} has grav and cubic anomalies of -1 without nu_R and all six coefficients 0 with nu_R, so it is gaugeable. B2: 't Hooft counting gives Delta B = Delta L = N_f Delta N_CS = 3 and Delta(B-L) = 0, with N_f = 3 from PDG 2026 N_nu = 2.996 +- 0.007. This agrees with the READ restatements. B3: the full SU(2) Skyrme density -(1/24 pi^2) eps Tr(L L L) for a hedgehog equals -(sin^2 F F')/(2 pi^2 r^2) at 4 random points (max deviation 5.2e-18). The degree is n for F(0) = n pi, n = -3..3. On the closed S^3 the map chi -> n chi has degree n, n = 0..4, and vol(S^3) = 2 pi^2 != 0, so the volume form is closed but not exact. The Gauss density div grad(cos chi) integrates to 0, which is exact. So closure quantises B but does not fix its value. B4: z3 on a periodic 3^3 lattice (81 integer links). With the Gauss constraint, total != 0 is UNSAT for every integer link field; the vacuity guard (nonzero local charge) is SAT. A global number with no Gauss constraint has total = 1 SAT. B5: eta = 6.125e-10 from Omega_b h^2 = 0.0224. Omega_K = 0.001 +- 0.002 admits both open and closed. For a massive (Higgsed) gauged B-L on T^3, a uniform net charge solves -lap A0 + m^2 A0 = rho with A0 = rho0/m^2. (One expectation in the first run had the wrong sign for the B-L grav/cubic anomaly in the LH basis. The script's expected value was corrected to -1; the computed values were never changed.) NOTE, not a finding: 2505.05607 eq.(48) gives the anomaly 'of the form' with only the SU(2) term. B1's Y^2 B = -1/2 shows a hypercharge term also exists. The paper says 'of the form', so this is a restriction of scope, not an error.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. No numerical datum enters 'closure does not force B'. It follows from the absence of a Gauss constraint, and B1 shows that absence is forced within the SM by anomaly consistency (U(1)_B cannot be gauged with SM fermions, with or without nu_R). What earlier physicists lacked was not data against this. Data that came later only corroborates the premises: N_f = 3 is now PDG 2026 2.996 +- 0.007 (it fixes Delta B = 3 and leaves 'not forced' untouched), and the observed eta = 6.1e-10 != 0 is consistent with 'not forced'. Two open inputs could change the picture. (a) Discovery of a massless gauge boson coupled to B-L, which becomes anomaly-free once nu_R exists, and nu_R is motivated by the neutrino-mass data that came after the 1976 anomaly result. Closure would then force B_total = L_total (H2). Current torsion-balance bounds constrain but do not exclude this (NAMED-NOT-READ). (b) Nonperturbative quantum-gravity results on closed universes (2501.02359, NAMED-NOT-READ), which are theory, not data, and contested. Neither is evidence that the result is wrong on its hypotheses. Both are reasons it holds on a narrower class than 'no topological constraint' suggests.
grade_evidence: THE CORE BOOLEAN STANDS ON ITS HYPOTHESES, and it is re-derived exactly here. Without a Gauss constraint, a nonzero total is admissible on a closed slice: B4 is a z3 universal UNSAT/SAT pair on the same periodic lattice, and B3 gives degree-n configurations on S^3 for every tested n. B1 computes that within the SM U(1)_B cannot carry a Gauss law, because it is anomalous: SU(2)^2 B = 1/2, Y^2 B = -1/2. THE TREE'S STATEMENT-AS-USED IS WIDER THAN THE RESULT on three counts. (1) 'No topological constraint' (permute.py:346) is too strong. B's changes are locked to Chern-Simons winding, Delta B = 3 Delta N_CS (B2, READ 2505.05607 p.6 and 1710.07223 p.1). In the Skyrme realisation B is an integer topological degree on a closed slice (B3). Topology quantises B; it does not fix B. (2) Premise H2 is unnamed at permute.py:132-134, :346 and :562-564. With nu_R, U(1)_{B-L} is anomaly-free (B1). If it were gauged with a massless untwisted boson, closure would force B_total = L_total, a constraint on B. A massive boson forces nothing (B5). (3) H3 is unnamed: the SM does not conserve B at all, only B-L. The baryon row is asserted data; permute.py's selftest never checks it (permute.py:466-472). NOT WRONG: nothing here refutes 'closure does not force B' within the SM on a fixed background. NOT DATA-DEPENDENT: no datum has moved against it (N_f and eta only corroborate; closure itself is undecided, Omega_K = 0.001 +- 0.002). NOT STANDS: the gloss as written overstates, and the operative premise is unnamed. DOWNSTREAM, recorded and not repaired: the row contradicts the universal reading of apply.py:91 ('A SIGN-BLIND QUANTITY ... IS CONSTRAINED BY CLOSURE'), since B is sign-indefinite and unforced. The discriminator is the Gauss constraint, not the sign. The direction apply.py:252 uses (sign-committed energy is not constrained) does not move. CAVEAT: no originating statement exists to read. The anomaly limb is READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT; the quantum-gravity and torsion-balance literature is NAMED-NOT-READ (alphaXiv quota exhausted; arXiv egress-blocked).
